::: {#exr-bat-send-chair}
The core modeling functions take pure numbers (dimensionless) as input and produce pure numbers as output. To use them with real-world quantities that have units, we use **input transformations**. 

An input transformation has the form $a(q - q_0)$ where $q$ is the real-world input quantity. What must be true about the dimension of $q_0$?

```{devoirs_choices}
#| label: choices_d06.bsc.esd
- 'It must be dimensionless':
    correct: false
- 'It must have the same dimension as $q$':
    correct: true
- 'It must have the reciprocal dimension of $q$':
    correct: false
- 'It can have any dimension':
    correct: false
```
